sources.citation: Riley, E. Baxter (with introduction and notes by Sidney H. Ray). 1930. Sixteen vocabularies from the Fly River, Papua. Anthropos 25(1-2): 173-194 (intro) and 25(5-6): 831-850 (Dorro and Parb vocabularies).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Introduction places 'Parb.. west of the Wasi Kasa river. Also on Strachan Island and the Mai Kasa'; the vocabulary pages are a bare wordlist (scanned column-garbled in the copy we hold).

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1923. The languages of the Western Division of Papua. Journal of the Royal Anthropological Institute 53: 332-360.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Groups Dungerwab, Dapo and Parb as the 'Parb Group' (Wasi Kasa River, Strachan Island, Mai Kasa); 'Note on Orthography' only says spelling follows the Annual Reports / RGS rules; grammar notes give Parb noun suffixes and 'go' paradigm.

sources.citation: Ray, Sidney H. 1907. Reports of the Cambridge Anthropological Expedition to Torres Straits, vol. III: Linguistics. Cambridge: CUP. Section 'Papuan languages, West: 3. Dungerwab', pp. 293-295 (sketch based on the 1895-96 Annual Report vocabulary).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The 'Phonology' paragraph (p. 293) lists only vowels ('a, aa, e, i, o, ö.., u') and consonants and spelling conventions; no accent/stress remark. Usher identifies Dungerwab with Län; pronoun 'yond' = I matches the ASJP Len list.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page lenn1234 (Len) and namo1249 (Namo-Len); ASJP list LEN_1 (source: Anonymous 1896, BNG Annual Report 1895-96: 106-120, contributed by M. S. Dryer).
sources.note: Glottolog lists zero descriptive references (only Evans et al. 2018 as a subclassification comment; AES moribund). The ASJP entry confirms the 1896 Dungerwab wordlist is the only lexical source in circulation.

sources.citation: Usher, Timothy. New Guinea World: East Morehead River (= Nambu) family page, 'Sources' inventory; and the Län page (empty stub).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No stress content; it is the source inventory that identifies Dungerwab (Anon. 1895-96), Dapo (Lyons 1913-14), Parb (Ray 1923; Riley 1930-31) and Tuj (Williams 1936) as Län, and lists Evans (2015) comparative vocabulary of Len of Tais village in Carroll ed. (2015) (unpublished).

sources.citation: Evans, Nicholas et al. 2018. The languages of Southern New Guinea. In Bill Palmer (ed.), The Languages and Linguistics of the New Guinea Area, 641-774. De Gruyter Mouton.
